messages:
Sam Walker: Quick heads-up — ran a full profiling sweep on the 8xA100 PP/TP experiment with activation checkpointing ON. Seeing a ~35% p99 token latency regression vs no-checkpoint baseline. Flame graphs point to all-reduce stalls during recompute windows. :thinking:

Sam Walker: Repro config: TP=2, PP=4, model ~7B, micro-batch=2, global_bs=16, seq_len=2048, checkpointing=stagewise (every layer block). KV cache warm.

Sam Walker: Key profiler snippets (simplified):
```
compute_time: 42ms
allreduce_time: 28ms  # spikes during recompute phases
idle/comm_wait: 18ms
percent_comm_of_step: 40%   # up from 12% baseline
```

Lee Chen: Oof. Did you capture NCCL trace? Are we seeing small all-reduce buckets due to checkpointing breaking the forward pipeline?

Sam Walker: Yeah NCCL traces attached in the perf bucket link (perf-bot posted). Looks like a lot of tiny all-reduces interleaved with recompute. When PP stage recomputes it serializes work and triggers frequent grad all-reduces.

Maria Gomez: Is KV cache involved? We sometimes broadcast small KV shards at each step which can inflate comm count if not aggregated.

Sam Walker: KV cache is warm and pinned to stage owners, but I think main issue is gradient sync. KV broadcasts are <5% here.

Aj Patel: Two quick ideas: (1) increase micro-batch so compute>comm ratio, (2) increase all-reduce bucket size / use hierarchical all-reduce to amortize overhead. Also try NCCL envs: NCCL_BUFFSIZE_BYTES=134217728 and NCCL_COLLNET_ENABLE=1 for our infra.

Cheng Li: Checkpointing tradeoff: more recompute -> less memory but more recompute-phase comm serialization. For PP/TP mix, recompute breaks the natural overlap windows between local compute and global all-reduce. Might need to move from layerwise checkpoint to stage-level checkpointing.

Lee Chen: Agree. Stage-level checkpoint reduces recompute frequency across PP boundaries, but increases peak mem. Could test toggling checkpoint granularity. Also test overlap knobs: set NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=0 and try enabling NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVL to favor p2p where possible.

perf-bot: Profiling URL: https://perf.internal/reports/1748000001 (contains flame graphs, nvprof logs, NCCL traces) :eyes:

Maria Gomez: Also think about kernel selection: recompute changes op shapes (smaller matmuls). If we fall back to non-fused kernels we lose TFLOPS and that amplifies comm ratio. Check that the autokernel selector keeps fused attention/ffn for recompute shapes.

Sam Walker: Good point — I saw a switch to fp16->bf16 fused kernels mismatch during recompute path. I'll dump kernel selection logs.

Aj Patel: Experiment plan proposal (short):
1) Run baseline with checkpoint=off (done)
2) Run checkpoint=stage-level, micro-batch=2 (current) -> measure allreduce% and p99
3) Same as (2) but micro-batch=4 and NCCL_BUFFSIZE_BYTES=134217728
4) Same as (2) but disable checkpoint for cross-PP layers only (partial recompute)
5) Instrument kernel selector during (2-4) to capture fallback events

Cheng Li: Add one more: try activation recompute regrouping where we recompute within TP groups rather than across PP boundaries. That might reduce inter-stage comms.

Lee Chen: I'll own (3) and (5). Sam, can you run (2) and (4)? Maria, can you add kernel selector traces on each run? Aj, Cheng — help interpret NCCL traces if things look weird.

Sam Walker: Yep I can run (2) and (4) today. Will paste logs here.

Sam Walker: Quick snippet of a config change I'm trying:
```
# run config override
parallel: { tp:2, pp:4 }
training: { micro_batch:4, checkpointing: "stage" }
env: { NCCL_BUFFSIZE_BYTES: 134217728 }
```

Maria Gomez: If we see kernel fallbacks, try forcing the fast gemm kernel with KERNEL_HINT=fast_gemm for a run — just to isolate whether kernel selection is the multiplier for comm overhead.

Aj Patel: Also consider increasing gradient accumulation steps so we do all-reduce less often (if latency budget allows). That's cheap to test.

Sam Walker: Ran (2) quick run; preliminary numbers: p99 down from +35% to +12% vs baseline; allreduce% dropped from 40% -> 22%. Kernel traces still show occasional fallback at recompute boundaries.

Lee Chen: Nice. That suggests checkpoint granularity was the main driver. Let's see kernel traces — if fallbacks coincide with recompute windows, then we need to update kernel selector to consider recompute-shape distributions during planning.

Cheng Li: Tradeoff note for later doc: We should add a heuristic that when PP depth > 2, prefer stage-level checkpointing by default for online serving workloads. For batch/offline maybe different.

ops-bot: FYI creating ticket INF-4821 to track follow-ups and patch for kernel selector. Assigned to Maria + Lee. Deadline: 2025-01-15. :rocket:

Sam Walker: Thanks all — I'll upload the full traces and a quick HOWTO to reproduce. Next sync in #eng-runtime tomorrow to review microbench numbers. :thumbsup:
